clue.text: One mostly horrible meeting one in prison who doesn't fight?

definitions.note: a clause standing for a person, the non-combatant

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for a prison
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: vile means horrible
again the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A query about a nasty jail inmate who keeps out of fights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims VILE to VIL; I, VIL and I go 'in' CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outside the armed forces, a non-combatant, is the person who does not fight in a war.

clue.text: Accusation that's made by 5

definitions.meaning: an indictment, as when police lay one against a suspect
5-across is a duty or scale of fees, and such a schedule sets a fee to pay

explanation.walkthrough: The 5 refers to 5-across, a duty or schedule of fees.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a formal allegation of crime and a price levied, the sort a schedule of duties imposes.

clue.text: Participants in democracy strove for change

indicators.note: for change says these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Citizens in a democracy fought hard for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges STROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Those casting ballots at elections are the people who take part in a democratic system.

clue.text: Man presenting stars with something aromatic

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars
nard, or spikenard, is an aromatic plant and ointment

explanation.surface: A fellow arrives with constellations and perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: NARD (spikenard) is a fragrant balm known from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for any male person, in the usual crossword way.

clue.text: A boss, frequently I'm ending with employee earlier than expected

parts.note: the head is the boss of an organisation
oft is an old word for often, frequently
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word for the worker

explanation.surface: A manager keeps saying they are finishing up with a staff member before the scheduled time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last letter of 'employee', E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done before the planned hour has come in advance of schedule, sooner than anticipated.

clue.text: Duty of sailor if meeting head of fleet

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word for the navy group

explanation.surface: A sailor's obligation if he meets the fleet's commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes F from 'fleet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A customs duty is a levy on imports, which a schedule of such charges sets out.

clue.text: Hostile to profits made in heartless act

indicators.note: in puts the profits word inside what is left of the deed
heartless removes the central letter of the word for a deed

parts.note: gains are profits

explanation.surface: Opposed to gains won through a cruel deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle C out of ACT, leaving AT; GAINS goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is being set against it, a straightforward synonym for the preposition.

clue.text: Fashionable character actually appearing

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a character in a story is a person

explanation.surface: A trendy figure really showing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being physically present yourself rather than by letter or video is the phrase's meaning.

clue.text: Big record about a person who has given up hope?

definitions.text: person who has given up hope?

indicators.note: about says the two words go round the letter that follows

parts.note: fat means big
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A huge record concerning someone who has abandoned hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' works on the joined pair, which wraps the lone letter so it ends up in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resigned to fate believes what will be will be, so the question mark admits it is a loose description.

clue.text: 'A superior and thunderous character,' journalist wrote

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior
Thor is the Norse god of thunder
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer's quoted description of a grand and booming figure.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To have penned a book or article is to have been its writer, its creator.

clue.text: Vehicle to fondle, something that can move magically?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to pet is to stroke or fondle

explanation.surface: A car to caress, an object able to travel by magic?
explanation.definitionFit: The flying rug of the Arabian Nights is the floor covering that travels by enchantment.

clue.text: Cloth around light forming a sort of decoration

indicators.note: around turns the cloth word backwards

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
to light is to land or alight, as a bird does

explanation.surface: Fabric wrapped round a lamp to make an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns RAG backwards; 'light' is the verb, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of flowers hung or worn as an ornament is a festive adornment.

clue.text: Trick by unwanted surfer endlessly achieving dominance

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the online pest

parts.note: a troll is an unwelcome internet user posting to provoke

explanation.surface: A trick played by an online pest who wins mastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims TROLL to TROL; 'surfer' means someone surfing the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Having power or command over something is having the upper hand, mastery of it.

clue.text: Policy to restrict men — no it can't, unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters fall out in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A rule to hold men back is said surprisingly to be impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges MEN NO IT CANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War strategy of keeping a rival's power from spreading was a policy of restriction.

clue.text: Components of clues one fits in, I'd fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb of imagining signals the letters being reworked

explanation.surface: A crossword fan imagines one piece slotting into place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ONE FITS IN ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cryptic clue contains a meaning element, the part that tells you what the solution means.

clue.text: Rules for conduct given quiet respect somehow

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Codes of behaviour delivered with hushed reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral maxims or principles guiding behaviour are guidelines on how to act.

clue.text: Celebrate around recreation ground — with fireworks doing this?

definitions.note: a description of what fireworks do, a verb form

indicators.note: around places the singing word round the grounds

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate in song
a park is a recreation ground

explanation.surface: A party in the park with fireworks going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the celebrating word wrapping the grounds; the definition is the whole closing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireworks give off flashes of bright fragments, throwing out tiny burning particles as they go.

clue.text: Party people about to meet hosts offering drinks

parts.note: re means about or concerning
publicans run pubs and serve drinks

explanation.surface: Revellers about to meet landlords serving drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: PUBLICANS are British pub landlords.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the US Grand Old Party are its supporters, people in one political party.

clue.text: Small animal or insect imbibing fizzy drink

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the insect holds the wine

parts.note: a bee is an insect
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A little creature or bug sipping a sparkling drink.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE is 'imbibing' ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word, familiar from Burns, for a little creature or critter.

clue.text: Offended about article giving words of derision

indicators.note: about puts the aggrieved word round the article

parts.note: sore means offended or aggrieved
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone hurt by a newspaper piece answers with mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: SORE goes 'about' THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish taunt said after winning a point, a phrase of triumphant scorn.

clue.text: Knight presents English bishop with a set of holy books

definitions.note: from knight-errant, the wandering knight of romance

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title
NT is the New Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A knight hands over books from the Bible to an English bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the phrase knight-errant; RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A roving knight in medieval romance was called a knight-errant, so the adjective stands for him.

clue.text: Top worker to criticise manager ultimately

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the boss word

explanation.surface: A senior employee should criticise the boss in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R from 'manager'. 'Top' is the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays roof tiles works at the top of a house.

clue.text: Work involved in transporting paintings etc. in compartment

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the business of carrying goods

indicators.note: in puts the paintings inside the enclosure

parts.note: a cage is an enclosed compartment
art covers paintings and the like

explanation.surface: Moving artworks in a crate takes effort.
explanation.walkthrough: ART goes 'in' CAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The conveying of goods by cart or vehicle, and the charge for it, is haulage.

clue.text: Raw note

definitions.meaning: raw means unprocessed, in its native state
in music a note that is neither sharp nor flat

explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined things are in their original state; in music a plain unaltered pitch is marked with the same word.

clue.text: News incorporates four of these critical comments

definitions.meaning: the letters N, E, W, S are compass directions
remarks made in argument or critique

explanation.walkthrough: The four letters of NEWS are North, East, West and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass directions are cardinal markers, and arguments put forward in debate are remarks made.

clue.text: Funny tales etc. featured in what's seen on the box

indicators.note: funny means odd, signalling the letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: Amusing stories turn up on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' rearranges TALES ETC. 'The box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast programme is what viewers watch on their television sets.

clue.text: Number of US soldiers in retreat making an impression

definitions.note: a phrase for the thing that makes an impression, a seal

indicators.note: in retreat turns the number and soldiers backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A troop of American soldiers falling back yet impressing people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns TENGIS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal on a ring pressed into wax leaves a mark, an impression.

clue.text: Witness attending examination in front of soldiers

indicators.note: in front of places the exam ahead of the soldiers

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a test is an examination
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A witness present at a test before the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) means soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: One who certifies or vouches for something, as a signatory does, bears witness.
